full_judgment:
c. Baluster of claim put forth by plaintiff was that he took settlement of suit tank plot No. 596 from Maharaja of Tripura by way of registered Patta deed dated 9-4-1951 and got possession thereof. 

 n. Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh represented by Deputy Commissioner, Comilla once again mounted an endeavour to re-open controversy on institution of a suit being Title Suit No. 165 of 1985 in the Third Court of Munsif (now Assistant Judge), Comilla seeking a declaration that alleged lease of suit land by Abdur Razzak from Maharaja of Tripura by an unilateral patta executed on 9-4-1951 and registered on 12-4-1951 is illegal, malafide, collusive, without jurisdiction, void and is of no legal effect and right, title and interest of plaintiff on suit land is not effected by it. 

 i. Title of first-defendant-petitioner had been declared and possession had been confirmed on suit tank in Title Suit No. 136 of 1951 as well as title Suit No. 467 of 1977 and decision rendered in both the suits in respect of acquisition of Title on the part of predecessor of first-defendant-petitioner on the strength of Patta deed from Maharaja of Tripura had been confirmed by High Court Division as well as Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh and present suit is hit by the principle of res judicata and, also, of constructive res judicata and controversy, which was laid at rest finally by highest court of land i.e. Appellate Division, cannot be allowed to be re-opened by plaintiff-opposite party on laying a fraudulent, misconceived and fancy suit. 

 13. In suit in hand relief claimed by plaintiff-opposite party i.e. Government of Bangladesh, is that alleged lease of suit land by Abdur Razzak from Maharaja of Tripura by a unilateral patta executed on 9-4-1951 registered on 12-4-1951 is illegal, malafide, collusive, without jurisdiction, void and is of no legal effect and right, title and interest of the plaintiff is not affected by it. In Title Suit No. 136 of 1959 foundation of claim of Abdur Razzak, predecessor of defendant-petitioner was, patta deed dated 9-4-1951 from Maharaja of Tripura in respect of Suit Tank and title on suit tank had been declared by Court of First Instance. The said Judgment was, also, upheld in the Appeal carried by Government. Government remains fully satisfied with Judgment and decree and did not carry the issue neither before High Court Division nor before Appellate Division. In Title Suit No. 467 of 1977 the order passed by Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) acquiring the suit tank was struck down by the learned Appellate Judge in Title Appeal No. 154 of 1980 and the verdict pronounced in Title appeal was maintained by the High Court Division as well as by Appellate Division. The patta deed dated 9-4-1951 in favour of predecessor of defendant-petitioner by Maharaja of Tripura was accepted as valid patta deed by highest court of the land. Venture undertaken from the side of plaintiff-opposite party i.e. Government of Bangladesh, to reopen the issue which was finally and conclusively decided by judicial verdicts of last and highest Court of the country, cannot be allowed to be proceeded with and attempt by way of a presentation of a plaint is liable to be nipped in the bud at its inception so that no further time is consumed on a fruitless litigation.
